feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: it presents a clear leadership narrative, solid platform expertise, and relevant scale indicators. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly repetitive and overpacked, with some structural duplication and a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary quickly establish a focused brand in digital platforms, governance, communications systems, and AI-enabled experiences.  
- Good evidence of impact: metrics such as 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, and 50+ internal publishers strengthen credibility.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, multimedia, and operations align well with the target leadership profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and more space for achievements.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in consulting and earlier roles (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement growth, adoption, cost savings).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler; maintain consistent punctuation/hyphenation across bullets and terms like “front-end/front end,” “organization-wide,” and date formatting (“Oct.”/“Sept.”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground scale/relevance: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector digital platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Add 1–2 concrete signals of scope from recent roles, e.g., “enterprise web modernization for 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace “behind high-volume public-sector communications” with more direct outcome-oriented phrasing such as “supporting large-scale public-sector communications and advocacy.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for mission-driven public-sector organizations. Builds scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and digital performance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories slightly more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for cleaner readability.
- Emphasize higher-level leadership capabilities over task-level wording like “operations.”
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve more technical terms for Topline Skills/Technical + IT and keep this section strategic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat almost verbatim from the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening the wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more additive and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize distinct value: e.g., “AI Hybrid Search: Shaped an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”
- Replace generic phrasing like “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper language such as “built on a modular Drupal 10 architecture for reuse and expansion.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across all entries; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency in formal CV writing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work closely mirror bullets in the 2024–present and 2018–2024 experience sections.
- Consider keeping only the most differentiated projects here or adding outcomes not mentioned elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, distinctive deliverables, and current impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Advised,” “Built,” “Led,” “Improved,” “Launched.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, engagement lift, or stakeholder teams served.
- Separate strategy from execution: one bullet for governance/workflows/analytics, one for Drupal microsites and front-end delivery, one for AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats the 2022–2024 director entry unless tied to new consulting deliverables.
- Microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep the CV item higher-level and let projects hold the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the most senior-level achievements without repeating themes covered in the consultant and prior NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in email/social engagement, production volume from the studio, reporting efficiency, or governance adoption/compliance.
- Combine softer bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and formalized publishing governance, standards, and cross-department planning to improve content quality and operational consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the consultant role and Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-program expansion overlaps with the earlier NACo role; keep focus here on building the studio and scaling organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership: newsletters, advocacy video, and cross-team editorial operations.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operational point: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is very similar to the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this role focused on execution/operations, not overall leadership.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and emphasize governance/enterprise scope over broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more distinctive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content strategy and campaign planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder-focused public-sector communications” if you want a less repetitive, more executive tone.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-led phrases, 4 bullets max, no filler adjectives.
- If possible, align one phrase to measurable scope elsewhere (e.g., “enterprise web and content operations for 10,000+ page platforms”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep this section broader and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to enterprise web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” is stronger than listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search, front-end implementation.
- Trim lower-signal or older-feeling items unless essential for target roles; consider dropping jQuery and possibly Airtable from this topline section.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and platform integrations • Workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep topline skills broader and more strategic, with detailed tools left below.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or remove from one section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not repeat the software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, performance and user-behavior analysis”
- Put the strategic outcomes first: KPI design, executive reporting, decision support, optimization.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboarding and reporting” and “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this section higher-level and leave the full tool list there.
- GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading this item with the same sequence.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo experience bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, more distinctive capabilities rather than generic production terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level to capability-level language: “Broadcast studio leadership” is stronger than “Video production and editing.”
- Use a tighter version such as:
- Broadcast studio leadership
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ and multi-camera production systems
- Virtual event and webcast operations
- If accurate, replace one generic item with a scale/complexity cue, e.g. “Broadcast-quality in-house studio operations” or “Recurring advocacy video and event production.”
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and activities in the same list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase here.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already supported by recent NACo bullets, so this section should complement them, not restate them.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add context on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing instead of a bare list: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to be more outcome-oriented: **CMS & Web Platform Administration**
- If you want stronger impact, align with recent work: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed version in one place only.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the rest; remove it unless it supports a visible project or portfolio use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)**
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes instead of only tools, e.g. **Built front-end components, implemented tracking via GTM, automated deployments with GitHub Actions, and developed edge/serverless integrations with Cloudflare Workers**
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5/CSS3**) unless the rest of the CV uses versioned naming; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**
- **API integrations** and broader technical execution are also implied in recent NACo roles; avoid repeating the same phrasing across sections

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more role-relevant by emphasizing automation platforms over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and prioritize higher-signal tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira” before project/chat tools.
- Consider renaming to: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” if you keep Slack/Teams/Asana.
- Tighten the list to the most relevant tools for your recent work: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams.”
- If space allows elsewhere, add light context instead of more tools, e.g., “workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial coordination” rather than listing every PM platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating too many adjacent terms.
- Basecamp and Trello feel lower-value/redundant unless used recently or materially.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal scale or use case, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**.
- Tighten and standardize product naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a brief qualifier to connect tools to recent work, e.g. **used for newsletter operations, audience engagement, and campaign communications**.
- Best stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email newsletter operations, member engagement, and campaign communications**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email/newsletter channels; avoid repeating audience-size claims here unless you remove them from role descriptions.
- “Engagement” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ multi-channel communications language, so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In a technical section, it should emphasize methods and implementation depth rather than repeat the same platform names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and sharpen the list: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **“Dashboarding”** with a stronger capability term such as **“KPI reporting”** or **“performance reporting”**
- If accurate, add one higher-signal implementation skill from recent work: **measurement strategy**, **event tracking**, **reporting infrastructure**, or **analytics QA**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping tools here and moving broader capabilities there.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid expanding this list into narrative claims without outcomes.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, or frequency of weekly updates.
- Tighten the second sentence around outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s daily work.”
- If accurate, add impact language such as improved publishing speed, expanded in-house production capacity, or increased consistency across channels.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; position this as the initial team/process foundation.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the distinct innovation/research scope and keep the multimedia point concise.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to foreground coordination + launch impact: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the digital sentence: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational initiatives, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Consider a two-bullet format for clarity: one bullet on innovation/research support, one on podcast/content production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overemphasize multimedia leadership here; later roles show larger-scale video/studio ownership more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, not broad capabilities already demonstrated elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Tighten to software/platforms and make labels more specific:  
  **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- Replace broad phrases with more concrete tool/process language if true:  
  **OBS / livestream control workflows** or **Broadcast studio production workflows** instead of “Livestream studio workflows”
- Consider reframing “Podcast production” as a capability with scope if you can support it elsewhere:  
  **Podcast recording, editing & post-production**
